environment.description: Same build service container deployed on EKS 1.29 with Bottlerocket AMI nodes. Pod spec includes: securityContext.seccompProfile.type=RuntimeDefault, runAsNonRoot=true (uid 1000), allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, readOnlyRootFilesystem=true (with emptyDir for /tmp/builds). Node-level Bottlerocket settings: kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0, kernel lockdown=integrity. Additionally, the EKS cluster has a Kyverno ClusterPolicy 'restrict-syscalls' that enforces the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile. The critical control: an OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate 'K8sBlockProcessExec' with a matching Constraint applied to the namespace, which intercepts all container process creation via the Falco runtime engine sidecar (falcosidekick -> OPA admission) and blocks any process whose argv[0] is not in the explicit allowlist ['/usr/local/bin/python3', '/usr/local/bin/flask', '/usr/bin/git', '/usr/bin/make']. The Falco rule 'Unexpected Spawned Process' with priority CRITICAL triggers on any execve not matching the allowlist, and falcosidekick is configured with a kill action (SIGKILL to the offending process within 50ms via the Kubernetes audit response). The subprocess.run with shell=True spawns /bin/sh which is NOT in the allowlist, causing immediate SIGKILL of the shell process before command execution completes.

config.falco_rules: Unexpected Spawned Process: condition (spawned_process and not proc.name in (python3, flask, git, make)) priority CRITICAL
